text:
The response is scientifically sound. It correctly identifies the polar vortex, the roughly −78°C threshold for polar stratospheric clouds, the conversion of chlorine reservoirs (HCl, ClONO₂) into Cl₂ on cloud surfaces, and sunlight-driven photolysis as the reason destruction waits for spring. It also covers the catalytic ozone loss and the late-spring vortex breakdown that refills the layer. Minor weaknesses: "stored chlorine is released" is loose wording for activation, and the text runs about 125–130 words, slightly over the 120-word limit.

Score: 8
